stories.title: Beyond the Headlines, CRE Is Thousands of Local Stories
stories.excerpt: Read the commercial real estate headlines and you would picture the market as rows of glass towers and mega-warehouses ringing a handful of big cities: distressed office high-rises, institutional write-downs, the occasional gateway-city megadeal. Big names, big cities, big bets, big wins and losses.  That may be the part that draws attention, but it’s not the market most of the industry works in. Vast logistics parks dominate industrial coverage, yet smaller facilities have historically held sub-5% vacancy. Properties with fewer than 50 units account for two-thirds of multifamily, according to an analysis of Census Bureau data. Spaces under 5,000 square feet now represent roughly 80% of retail leases, CoStar reports, while the average U.S. office requirement is about 3,500 square feet.  Transaction data reinforces the point. Altus Group found that even as median per-square-foot pricing across major property types reached new highs in the first quarter of 2026, the typical commercial transaction remained under $5 million. Excluding hospitality, that figure falls below $2 million.  At the top of the market, that’s a rounding error. Across the country, these are transactions that help communities thrive. It’s the local physician group buying a medical office building, or the craftsman operating out of a small warehouse space. It’s the corner walk-up apartment building, a neighborhood strip mall, or quaint motel off the main road. It’s the branded restaurant franchise that’s running on a local entrepreneur’s personal savings.   It’s a disconnect Kristie Kimnach knows well. As executive director of REMAX Commercial®, she leads a network of more than 17,600 commercial professionals and 559 commercial offices and divisions within the broader REMAX global network, which has a presence in more than 120 countries and territories.  “The fabric of commercial real estate is made up of thousands of local stories,” she says. “People see the tip of the
bullets: Two-thirds of multifamily stock is sub-50 units; median transaction under $2M excluding hospitality.
80% of retail leases under 5,000 sq ft; industrial sub-5% vacancy in smaller facilities.
Headline deals mask vast majority of CRE activity in local, smaller-scale transactions.
stories.summary: Industry data shows the bulk of commercial real estate—two-thirds of multifamily, 80% of retail leases, and smaller industrial—operates in transactions well below $5M, typically under $2M. This fragmented market of local deals drives community growth but receives minimal media coverage compared to megadeals in gateway cities.
stories.impact: Minimal. Article is meta-commentary on coverage patterns, not a market signal. No implications for development underwriting, demand, supply, or capital in specific markets.

stories.title: Capstone Equities Signs UK AI Tenant to First U.S. Location
stories.excerpt: Capstone Equities, its partners Rugby Realty and Republic Investment Company, and JLL announced today that Conduct AI will open its first U.S. office at 140 Crosby St., a boutique Class A office building in Manhattan’s SoHo neighborhood. The lease encompasses the entire 6,705-square-foot third floor and represents the first transaction at the property since Capstone Equities took ownership. Founded in London in 2024, Conduct is building an AI operating system for enterprise software, using agentic AI to help businesses understand, operate and transform complex enterprise systems. The company raised $60 million in its Series A funding round in June and is expanding its engineering and go-to-market teams as it grows internationally. Its new SoHo headquarters will mark its first permanent U.S. location and accommodate more than 60 employees. The transaction comes as Capstone Equities prepares to make new investments in the property, including a renovation of its communal rooftop deck.“Signing a fast-growing company like Conduct AI as our first new tenant speaks to the appeal of 140 Crosby and the kind of companies this property attracts,” said Daven Roshan, Director of Acquisitions at Capstone Equities. JLL Executive Managing Director Clark Finney, Director Alex Riguardi and Senior Associate Dana Goldman represented Capstone Equities. Max Mond and John Brennan of Savills represented Conduct AI. The post Capstone Equities Signs UK AI Tenant to First U.S. Location appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Conduct AI (London, $60M Series A June 2025) leases 6,705 sq ft SoHo Manhattan, first U.S. office.
Tech tenant seeking 60+ employees in boutique Class A; signals knowledge-worker demand in Manhattan.
Capstone Equities planning building renovations; asset repositioning underway.
stories.summary: Conduct AI, a London-founded AI software company that raised $60M in Series A funding in June 2025, has signed its first U.S. lease at 140 Crosby St. in Manhattan's SoHo neighborhood. The lease covers the entire 6,705-sq-ft third floor and is designed to accommodate 60+ employees as the company expands its engineering and go-to-market teams.
stories.impact: Limited direct multifamily relevance. However, it reinforces strong Manhattan knowledge-worker demand from well-capitalized AI/enterprise software firms. This signals sustained office leasing and potential worker housing demand in SoHo/NoMad, though the tenant base skews toward high-wage earners less likely to drive renter-occupied multifamily in outer boroughs.

stories.title: North Hollywood Apartments Trade to Locally Based LLC
stories.excerpt: Marcus & Millichap has finalized the sale of 13103 Barbara Ann St., a 41-unit multifamily property in North Hollywood. The property sold for nearly $5.89 million, or $143,610 per unit, and closed escrow at a 5.7% cap rate based on in-place income. “The property had been under the same ownership for more than 30 years, creating a rare opportunity to acquire an asset of this size with significant repositioning potential,” said Rick Raymundo, executive managing director investments. “As recent pricing volatility has eased, we’re seeing buyers move with more confidence on well-priced properties when sellers are committed to completing a transaction. This buyer plans to make common area and interior upgrades throughout the property.” Raymundo, in Marcus & Millichap’s Encino office, marketed the property on behalf of the seller, The Kwan Trust, and procured the buyer, a San Fernando Valley-based limited liability company. The post North Hollywood Apartments Trade to Locally Based LLC appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: North Hollywood, 41-unit sale at $143,610/unit, 5.7% cap rate; long-held asset repositioned.
Marcus & Millichap brokered; buyer is San Fernando Valley-based LLC planning upgrades.
Market signaling: pricing stabilization driving buyer confidence on well-priced value-add opportunities.
stories.summary: A 41-unit apartment building in North Hollywood, held by the same owner for 30+ years, sold for $5.89M ($143,610/unit) at a 5.7% cap rate. The locally-based buyer plans interior and common-area upgrades, with the broker citing renewed buyer confidence as pricing volatility has eased.
stories.impact: SAN FERNANDO VALLEY SIGNAL: 5.7% cap rate on value-add repositioning indicates strengthening buyer appetite for stabilized but upgradeable assets. With common-area renovation plans, buyer expects rent growth post-improvement; suggests confidence in underlying SFV rental demand and property-level NOI expansion. Watch for increased acquisition activity on aged, well-located multifamily stock in LA's secondary submarkets.

stories.title: Mojo Coffee Officially Opens in Chicago’s Loop
stories.excerpt: Mojo Coffee has officially opened at 70 W. Madison in Chicago’s Loop, taking over a ground-floor corner of the office tower owned and managed by partners, Namdar Realty Group and Mason Asset Management. The New Zealand-born specialty roaster joins over 244,000 square feet of leasing activity across the building in recent months, including significant lease extensions and new commitments. Since acquiring 70 W. Madison in December 2024 for $85 million, Namdar Realty Group and Mason Asset Management have continued to invest in various infrastructure modernization, building upgrade, and tenant improvement projects while expanding its occupancy. Mojo Coffee’s opening activates a prime 1,576-square-foot retail space with both street and direct lobby access. Mojo is replacing a roughly 1,500-square-foot Starbucks that exited the market as part of nationwide closures. Mojo also has cafes in Chicago at 190 South LaSalle Street, 200 South Wacker, and 330 N. Wabash Ave in River North. The post Mojo Coffee Officially Opens in Chicago’s Loop appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Mojo Coffee (New Zealand chain) replaces Starbucks at 70 W. Madison, Chicago Loop; 1,576 sq ft.
Namdar/Mason Asset acquired tower Dec 2024 for $85M; 244K+ sq ft leased recently.
Retail activation signals occupancy recovery and landlord confidence in Loop asset repositioning.
stories.summary: Mojo Coffee, a New Zealand specialty roaster, has opened at 70 W. Madison in Chicago's Loop, occupying a corner ground-floor retail space vacated by Starbucks as part of nationwide closures. The building, acquired by Namdar Realty and Mason Asset Management in December 2024 for $85M, has achieved 244,000+ sq ft in recent leasing activity and is undergoing infrastructure and tenant improvement upgrades.
stories.impact: CHICAGO LOOP: Retail activation of 1,576 sq ft (replacing Starbucks) in a recently stabilized office tower indicates rising foot traffic and occupancy confidence post-acquisition. This supports narrative that Loop office and ancillary demand is recovering. Adjacent residential demand in downtown/River North may benefit from improved amenity packages and user experience in trophy office buildings, though office-to-residential conversion remains the larger story.

stories.title: Charney Companies, Tavros Break Ground on Fifth Gowanus Development
stories.excerpt: Charney Companies and Tavros recently celebrated the groundbreaking of 175 Third St. in Gowanus, Brooklyn. The 27-story mixed-use tower, the newest addition to the Gowanus Wharf development, will house more than 1,000 apartments, approximately 250 of them affordable. Designed by Bjarke Ingels Group (BIG) and dencityworks, the project will also include a 28,000-square-foot public waterfront esplanade designed by Field Operations. 175 Third St. is the fifth development in the neighborhood by the co-developers, who are known for Gowanus Wharf, which brings 2,200 total units to the area. Pictured, from left: Nicholas Silvers, Tavros; Dov Barnett, Tavros; Colin Rankowitz, Tavros; Justin Pelsinger, Charney Companies; Sam Charney, Charney Companies;and Sam Sparks, Tavros. The post Charney Companies, Tavros Break Ground on Fifth Gowanus Development appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Charney Companies & Tavros break ground on 175 Third St., Gowanus, Brooklyn: 27-story, 1,000+ units.
250 units affordable; designed by Bjarke Ingels Group; part of Gowanus Wharf (2,200 total units).
Fifth development by co-developers; major supply pipeline addition to Brooklyn waterfront.
stories.summary: Charney Companies and Tavros have broken ground on 175 Third St. in Gowanus, Brooklyn—a 27-story mixed-use tower featuring 1,000+ apartments (250 affordable) and a 28,000-sq-ft public waterfront esplanade. It is the fifth development by the co-developers in Gowanus and part of the larger Gowanus Wharf project totaling 2,200 units.
stories.impact: BROOKLYN/GOWANUS SUPPLY PIPELINE: This project adds 1,000+ units to an already dense development corridor. Combined with co-developers' prior 2,200 units, the market is experiencing significant below-market (250 affordable) and market-rate supply influx. Rental demand absorption and rent growth potential in Gowanus will hinge on net migration and job growth in the metro; expect rents to moderate if supply outpaces demand. Monitor lease-up pace and rent trends closely to assess feasibility of new competing projects in Williamsburg/Greenpoint.

stories.title: Kolter, BH Inch Toward Buyout on Oceanfront Miami Beach Condo
stories.excerpt: Developers Kolter Group and BH Group are almost done assembling their oceanfront site in Miami Beach, with plans to redevelop it into a luxury condo complex. The joint venture now owns the majority of units within the Port Royale condo building at 6969 Collins Avenue in the North Beach neighborhood. Since July, it has paid $61.6 million for 163 units within the 172-unit building, according to an analysis of property records by data company Vizzda, first reported by the Business Journals. Five years ago, Port Royale residents were evacuated after the 55-year-old building was deemed unsafe, CBS Miami reported. The evacuation came after the deadly collapse of the nearby Champlain Towers South condo building in 2021. The condo sales are likely related to state reforms passed after 2021 that have increased building maintenance fees for many condo owners, some of whom are selling to developers. The recent purchases add to Kolter Group and BH Group’s assemblage, which spans about 2 acres along the oceanfront between 69th and 71st streets and includes two neighboring hotels. Starting in 2023, Kolter purchased the 34,980-square-foot Normandy Plaza Hotel for $18 million. Located at 6985 Collins Avenue, the three-story structure was built in 1950. This January, an entity tied to the joint venture paid $26 million for the four-story Crystal Beach Suites, which was built in 1936 at 6979 Collins Avenue. This July, it also purchased the 7,600-square-foot commercial condos within the building for $14.4 million. This week, Wells Fargo increased a loan tied to those properties to $83.2 million. The bank doubled the debt amount from a mortgage first issued in January. Last week, the developers filed plans to demolish the Normandy Plaza Hotel. In 2025, they filed plans to build a 37-unit condo development designed by Kobi Karp on a portion of the site. bullets: Kolter Group & BH Group own 163 of 172 units in Port Royale, Miami Beach (6969 Collins Ave).
Paid $61.6M since July for buyout; building unsafe post-2021 collapse, residents evacuated 2020.
Rising condo maintenance fees (post-2021 state reforms) driving sellers to liquidate to developers.
stories.summary: Developers Kolter Group and BH Group have acquired 163 of 172 units in the Port Royale condo building in North Beach, Miami, for $61.6M since July. The 55-year-old building was evacuated in 2020 after being deemed unsafe; the joint venture plans a luxury condo redevelopment. Recent unit sales are driven by rising state-mandated building maintenance fees post-Champlain Towers collapse.
stories.impact: MIAMI BEACH/NORTH BEACH SUPPLY & DEMAND: This land assembly signals developer confidence in Miami Beach luxury condo market despite affordability pressures. However, the underlying driver—forced condo owner liquidation due to state-mandated safety/maintenance fees—reflects structural headwinds in older condo buildings. This creates opportunity for new construction but also suggests potential supply headwinds in aging multifamily stock and upside in Class A development. Monitor if similar forced sales accelerate in other Florida aging condo buildings.

stories.title: Google Relocation Leads D.C.’s Office Market in Q3
stories.excerpt: Washington, D.C.’s office market held relatively steady in the third quarter, but the divide between trophy properties and the broader market was extended. Tenants leased about 1.8 million square feet during the quarter, roughly in line with the market’s five-year quarterly average, but down from the 2 million square feet leased in the second quarter, according to Savills. Overall availability ticked down to 24 percent, while trophy space availability remained below 10 percent. The average Class A asking rent inched up 2 pennies since the second quarter to $62.31 per square foot per year. That scarcity in premier space is prompting tenants — mostly law firms and government departments — to make decisions years ahead of lease expirations while encouraging landlords to reposition buildings, according to Savills. Sheppard signed the quarter’s largest law firm deal, relocating to 107,227 square feet at 2033 K Street NW, where the property is slated for an extensive redevelopment. Greenberg Traurig also renewed and expanded to 80,089 square feet at 2101 L Street NW. Google posted the quarter’s largest lease deal in a 210,000-square-foot consolidation move to 500 North Capitol Street NW. And the local D.C. government renewed for 164,110 square feet at 1050 First Street NE and for 74,924 square feet at 645 H Street NE both ranked among the quarter’s largest deals. Federal leasing, however, remains a weak spot. Savills said General Services Administration leasing volume is on pace to decline from 2025 with fewer transactions above 100,000 square feet through the first three quarters. Meanwhile, D.C.’s office inventory declined by 4.7 million square feet compared to the same time last year, falling to 118.1 million square feet, as office-to-resi conversions continue removing space from the market. Gregory Cornfield can be reached at gcornfield@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Washington D.C. office: 1.8M sq ft leased Q3 (5-yr avg), 24% availability, Class A below 10%.
Class A asking rent $62.31/sq ft/yr; trophy space scarcity forcing tenants to decide years ahead.
Google relocation and law firm expansion (Sheppard 107K sq ft, Greenberg Traurig 80K sq ft) driving leases.
stories.summary: Washington D.C.'s office market remained relatively stable in Q3 with 1.8M sq ft leased, roughly in line with the five-year average. Trophy-class space availability fell below 10%, while overall availability held at 24%. Class A asking rents edged up 2 cents to $62.31/sq ft/yr, with major tenants including Google, law firms (Sheppard, Greenberg Traurig), and government departments driving leasing decisions years in advance.
stories.impact: WASHINGTON D.C. HOUSING DEMAND SIGNAL: Google's office relocation and sustained law firm expansion indicate strong knowledge-worker in-migration and job growth in a tight labor market. This supports sustained multifamily rental demand in urban core and submarkets with reverse commutes (Arlington, Bethesda, Silver Spring). High asking rents and trophy-space scarcity also imply strong wage growth among office tenants, supporting rent growth potential in premium multifamily near tech/law office clusters.

stories.title: Bank of America, JLL Provide $276M Refi for SoCal Senior Housing
stories.excerpt: A Nexus Development affiliate has landed $276 million in refinancing for two senior housing communities with 395 units in Newport Beach, Calif. Property records show that Bank of America provided the $140 million loan for Vivante Newport Center, while JLL Real Estate Capital provided $136 million for Vivante Newport Mesa. JLL Capital Markets arranged and announced the financings for the owner on Friday, but declined to identify the lenders. The $140 million loan for the 99-unit Newport Center loan works out to roughly $1.4 million per unit, which is one of the largest financings on a per-unit basis in the senior housing industry’s history, according to JLL. The six-story property opened in 2022 on San Clemente Drive with restaurants, a cocktail bar, a fitness center, an indoor pool, a theater, a bowling alley and a golf simulator. It is also near Fashion Island and Hoag Hospital Newport Beach. Meanwhile, Vivante Newport Mesa includes 296 units across a 6.8-acre campus on Monrovia Avenue. The property opened in phases in 2013 and 2020 with a three-story building and a four-story building. It is near South Coast Plaza. JLL’s Greg Brown and Aaron Rosenzweig represented privately held developer Nexus Development. Gregory Cornfield can be reached at gcornfield@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Nexus Development refinances two senior housing properties (395 units) in Newport Beach, CA: $276M total.
Vivante Newport Center (99 units, 2022): $1.4M per unit financing; among highest senior-housing per-unit loans.
Vivante Newport Mesa (296 units, 2013–2020): $136M; properties amenity-rich (pools, bowling, golf simulator).
stories.summary: A Nexus Development affiliate has secured $276M in refinancing for two senior housing communities totaling 395 units in Newport Beach, California. Bank of America provided $140M for the 99-unit Vivante Newport Center (opened 2022), while JLL Real Estate Capital provided $136M for the 296-unit Vivante Newport Mesa. The $1.4M-per-unit loan on Newport Center ranks among the largest per-unit senior housing financings on record.
stories.impact: ORANGE COUNTY/SOUTHERN CALIFORNIA SENIOR HOUSING: $1.4M/unit refinancing on a 2022-vintage senior property signals strong lender confidence and capital availability for stabilized, amenity-rich senior housing. This supports development feasibility for new senior communities in affluent coastal CA markets. Rising per-unit loan sizes may also reflect inflation and improved rents, suggesting renter demand for premium senior housing remains robust despite aging populations. Could signal headwinds for less-amenitized legacy senior stock competing for the same demographic.

stories.title: Sony in Talks to Anchor Tishman Speyer’s 99 Hudson Boulevard
stories.excerpt: Sony is in negotiations to become the anchor tenant of Tishman Speyer’s planned 99 Hudson Boulevard in Hudson Yards, Commercial Observer has learned, and may already have a term sheet. Sony’s current U.S. headquarters is in the top 568,000 square feet of 11 Madison Avenue, but Sony, like other corporate occupiers, is looking for newer, bigger and more collaborative workplaces for its employees. Sony signed a lease in 2013 and moved to 11 Madison after selling its iconic 550 Madison Avenue headquarters in 2012 to Joseph Chetrit for $1.12 billion. Chetrit flipped it three years later for $1.4 billion to Olayan America, which completely redeveloped the tower, which features a distinctive Chippendale-style top designed by Philip Johnson and John Burgee. While Sony’s current location in vibrant NoMad next to Madison Square Park is hard to beat, there is simply no room to expand in the 30-story building. It was originally designed by Harvey Wiley Corbett and Dan Everett Wade in 1928 to hit 100 stories before the Great Depression stopped its ascent. The Art Deco tower was not completed until 1950 and is currently owned by SL Green Realty. It’s unclear how much space Sony is in talks for at 99 Hudson Boulevard. Savills’ Erik Schmall and Allyson Bowen are representing Sony in the negotiations, but did not respond to requests for comment. Tishman Speyer has proposed 99 Hudson Boulevard as a 48-story office building of roughly 1.256 million square feet. Public documents state the firm will start construction on Dec. 1. The planned tower will sit opposite the Javits Center on 11th Avenue between West 36th and West 37th streets and have unobstructed views of the Hudson River. Its primary address of 99 Hudson Boulevard would place its main lobby facing the new Bella Abzug Park. Constructed as an all-electric LEED Gold tower, it would not be ready for occupancy until around 2030. bullets: Sony in talks to anchor Tishman Speyer's 99 Hudson Boulevard, Hudson Yards, Manhattan.
Sony currently occupies 568K sq ft at 11 Madison Avenue (NoMad); seeking expansion and newer collaborative space.
Large corporate tenant decision signals Hudson Yards' competitive positioning for Manhattan HQ relocations.
stories.summary: Sony is in negotiations to become the anchor tenant at Tishman Speyer's planned 99 Hudson Boulevard in Hudson Yards, with a potential term sheet already in place. Sony currently occupies 568,000 sq ft atop 11 Madison Avenue in NoMad but is seeking larger, newer space with improved collaboration features for employees. The company sold its iconic 550 Madison Avenue HQ in 2012 and has been at 11 Madison since 2013.
stories.impact: MANHATTAN/HUDSON YARDS OFFICE DEMAND: Sony's potential relocation to Hudson Yards, a space designed for modern collaboration, reinforces the appeal of newer trophy office to major corporate tenants facing expansion constraints and employee expectations for upgraded amenities. In-migration of large corporate HQs to Hudson Yards could drive residential demand in adjacent Hells Kitchen and West Chelsea; monitor concurrent multifamily demand from Sony employee base (likely affluent, Manhattan-oriented) and potential increase in co-working and mixed-use residential demand in the submarket.

stories.title: Hines Promotes Adam Hines to Co-CEO Alongside Laura Hines-Pierce
stories.excerpt: Laura Hines-Pierce is still co-CEO of the family firm, but with a new counterpart in Adam Hines. Hines-Pierce ascended to the role of co-CEO of investment and development firm Hines in February 2022 alongside her father, Jeffrey Hines. But as the elder Hines moves into the role of the firm’s chairman, another family member is moving up. Effective Jan. 1, Adam Hines and Hines-Pierce will lead the day-to-day operations of the company and strategic trajectory in the years to come, according to Hines. In addition, Hines-Pierce will replace Jeffrey Hines as CEO and chair of the board of Hines Global Income Trust, while Adam Hines will join its board as a director. “Hines has always been at its best when we look beyond the current cycle and build for what comes next,” Jeffrey Hines said in a statement. “Laura has already been leading Hines as co-CEO for five years, and Adam has helped shape important parts of our growth across Europe, private wealth and capital formation. Their leadership is already visible in the firm and platform we have built.” Also switching up their roles at Hines are David Steinbach, who was promoted to become the firm’s first president, and Alfonso Munk, who was promoted from co-head of investment management and will replace Steinbach as Hines’ global chief investment officer. “Scale creates advantage only when it improves execution,” Steinbach said in a statement. “Our opportunity is to connect what our teams know across markets, strategies and functions so local insight becomes shared intelligence and firmwide capabilities create more opportunity on the ground.” Adam Hines was recognized for doubling Hines’ private wealth business during his time as chief of staff for the office of the CEO and senior managing director of the company. He joined Hines in 2017 after holding several analyst positions at Australian real assets management firm Dexus. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Adam Hines promoted to Co-CEO alongside sister Laura Hines-Pierce effective Jan. 1, 2025.
Jeffrey Hines transitions to chairman; Laura becomes CEO/chair of Hines Global Income Trust.
Generational leadership transition in major multifamily/mixed-use developer; signals long-term capital and strategy continuity.
stories.summary: Hines has promoted Adam Hines to Co-CEO alongside his sister Laura Hines-Pierce, effective January 1, 2025. Laura, who became co-CEO in February 2022, will now also serve as CEO and chair of Hines Global Income Trust. Jeffrey Hines, the founder and current co-CEO, is stepping into the role of chairman. The move reflects planned generational transition in one of the largest private real estate development firms.
stories.impact: Minimal direct market impact. However, leadership transition in a large, family-controlled developer signals stability and continuation of long-term capital deployment strategy. No change in development appetite, project pipeline, or capital allocation is evident. Watch for any strategic shifts in geography, asset class focus, or risk appetite under new leadership team.
